fidelity: F2a — Combustion + Flue-Gas Energy Balance + Lumped Thermal-Mass ODE
source: Basu, P. (2013) Biomass Gasification, Pyrolysis and Torrefaction, 2nd ed., Academic Press; van Loo & Koppejan (2008) Handbook of Biomass Combustion and Co-firing, Earthscan; Obernberger & Thek (2008) The Pellet Handbook; EN 303-5:2012; Jenkins et al. (1998) Prog. Energy Comb. Sci. 24, 47-81.

unit.name: Generic 50 kW Modulating Biomass (Wood-Pellet) Boiler — Physics-Lumped

Q_rated.note: Rated useful thermal output to water

LHV_dry_MJ_kg.note: Dry-basis LHV of wood pellets (EN ISO 18125)

moisture_content.note: Moisture mass fraction, wet basis; EN+ pellets <=0.10, chips 0.20-0.35 — PRESERVED moisture->LHV coupling from F1

h_fg_water.note: Latent heat of vaporisation of water at ~25 degC (Obernberger & Thek 2008)

stoich_afr.note: Stoichiometric dry air-fuel mass ratio for cellulosic biomass (Basu 2013, Table 3.x)

excess_air_ratio.note: Excess-air ratio lambda; 1.2-1.5 typical for biomass grate combustion (van Loo & Koppejan 2008)

cp_flue.note: Mean specific heat of biomass flue gas 20-200 degC (van Loo & Koppejan 2008, ~1.05-1.15)

cp_water.note: Specific heat of liquid water at ~60 degC (NIST/IAPWS, 4.18-4.19)

m_water.note: Lumped water/jacket thermal mass (water content of boiler block)

m_metal.note: Boiler steel/cast-iron mass participating in thermal inertia

T_flue_full.note: Flue-gas exit temperature at full load (higher than NG due to char/ash)

UA_water.note: Heat-transfer conductance combustion gas -> boiler water mass

combustion_efficiency.note: Fraction of fuel LHV released (1 - unburnt-carbon loss); biomass 0.97-0.99 (van Loo & Koppejan 2008)

tau_fuel.note: First-order fuel-feed / combustion lag time constant
